text:
We're in the early stages of a multi year Mac super cycle. 

This morning, $AAPL announced some Mac updates, including 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac models (M6 chips). Still waiting on the first touchscreen Mac announcement later this morning.

Pricing is unchanged today. Keep in mind that late in June they raised the price of the MacBook by 18% and the iMac by 16%.

My take: There is upside to the Mac over the next two years. Mac has gone from 8.6% of revenue in June 2025 to 9.5% in June 2026. Last quarter it grew 29%. The Street is expecting 12% y/y in Sep ’26, going to 6% growth in FY27 and FY28.

Most important: I believe we are in the early stages of a multi-year AI-powered hardware upgrade cycle. Consumers and businesses will need to buy new hardware, even at higher prices, to fully leverage AI. That’s good for Mac growth. I expect FY27 Mac to grow above 10% (Street at 6%) and FY28 above 10% (Street at 6%).

the $meta selloff due to equity dilution is really annoying

meta and google both did equity raises this year for about $100B each. they are the greatest businesses in the world.

google is flat ytd and meta is now red after peaking at $780.

they have both been opportunity costs, but not because they are small spec plays that you took a chance on...these are some of the greatest businesses in the world.

the fact that $nvda and $amd had to invest in $meta today also shows how much the chipmakers realize that these companies need cash and they will have to participate in financing these companies to make sure their chip sales are disrupted.

text:
On Agentic:

Amazon used to say that when it reduced webpage load time by 10%, sales rose 10%: humans are incredibly sensitive to any friction, and removing it drives usage.

Internally, I've been sharing the view that the power of agents is not "please book me a flight next Tuesday using such and such criteria."

That is high friction: I am doing the work of asking, defining, etc. I may as well just do it myself.

Rather, the agent is useful when it finds you and prompts:

"Good morning, Compound. I saw you emailed @AndrewYAVB about visiting him in NYC next week. I've checked flights and your favorite hotels; here are some great options. Let me know if you want to book one or if you'd like me to use different criteria. Do you also want me to look at restaurants near your hotel for dinner?"

Or:

"Hi Compound, I saw you paid your September Verizon bill for $200 for four lines. Xfinity offers nearly identical service for $100 a month. I doubt you care who your phone provider is, and I can switch your whole family to Xfinity without you lifting a finger or noticing. I'll keep monitoring for even better deals down the road. Shall I proceed with switching?"

We want proactive AI that doesn't require you to ask it to do things. Rather, it anticipates your needs because you trust it with access to your information and it KNOWS you.

A few companies are natively well positioned for this:

Tier 1: Apple, Microsoft, Google
Tier 2: Meta
Tier 3: OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon

en_summary: I was expecting the Big Bad Wolf, but the Anthropic $ANT S-1 actually read quite well. Mgmt bullish that scaling law improvements will continue. Recursive development closing the loop, 250 new features. Focus on Cyber Security, Health Care/Life Sciences, Legal, Finance, Robotics. Capital efficient, burned only around $6.5b. Net revenue retention 900% for 11,900 customers spending $100k+. Long $ANT via May 2023 Series C. Concerns for competitors in law, finance, SaaS, cyber.
text:
I was expecting the Big Bad Wolf, but the Anthropic $ANT S-1 actually read quite well. 

A few takeaways: 

- Mgmt is bullish that scaling law improvements will continue
- Recursive development is increasingly closing “the loop” in new model development and fueling an aggressive product development roadmap across numerous verticals.  $ANT called out 250 new features and capabilities that it just rolled out.
- Beyond Coding, $ANT highlighted a particular focus on the Cyber Security and Health Care/Life Sciences verticals, as well as Legal, Finance, and Robotics.  
- Its models are increasingly positioned across the price/value spectrum to better match customer needs and ward off competitors.

$ANT has been impressively capital efficient to date, burning only around $6.5 b to date.  Compute spend is poised to ramp as it grows, which will raise risks, but this in turn will likely increase the competitive moat of $ANT (and OpenAI) in the medium term given how much compute the two leading frontier labs will control.  Also, I was impressed with $ANT’s margins on inference and overall operating leverage.

Bears have focused on falling token prices.  I think that’s an error.  It is better to pay attention to enterprise spend levels, which are nascent and barely in the 2nd inning in most organizations.  $ANT’s net revenue retention for its 11,900 customers (spending $100k or more) is 900%.  Budgets are only going to grow from here and $ANT should capture a meaningful share of that.

$
